ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Politics and Principles of Dissent In a context in which digital technologies blur the distinction between public and private lives, it is critically important to understand the philosophical, political, and legal principles with reference to which political speech, protest, and dissent are protected in democratic societies. In this course, we will examine the historical development of these principles and the ways they have been invoked, contested, and revoked in various political and civil rights movements as well in legal battles over changing social norms. We will draw on the historical and philosophical background to analyze the particular challenges posed by digital technologies today.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Not intended for students with Freshman class standing.
